Humans since 1982 (@humanssince1982) is redefining the boundaries between time, movement, and art. This Stockholm-based studio, founded by Bastian Bischoff and Per Emanuelsson, crafts mesmerizing kinetic installations that transform the concept of a clock into something far beyond function. Their standout works, ClockClock 24 and A Million Times, are not just timepieces—they are dynamic sculptures where synchronized hands move in hypnotic patterns, forming abstract designs before seamlessly aligning to display the time. Rooted in their philosophy of “Form follows fascination,” their pieces bridge the worlds of art, design, and technology, challenging our perception of time as something rigid and linear. Exhibited in prestigious galleries and private collections worldwide, their work turns the everyday act of reading time into an experience—one that is fluid, captivating, and ever-changing.
